assumptions: The four populations sit where the method expects them: at the grid's thresholds, as k-means clusters, or near a labelled training well's.
limits: The methods disagree on droplets between populations; that disagreement measures how much the answer rests on the method.
Only k-nearest-neighbours can abstain (Rain); k-means partitions everything.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which population (NN, NP, PN, PP) does each two-channel ddPCR droplet belong to, under a fixed grid, k-means or a k-nearest-neighbour vote?

description: ddPCR droplet amplitudes to populations. For TWO targets, a four-way classification — NN, NP, PN, PP — under any of THREE published methods that answer different questions and none of which is a fallback for another. `grid` applies eight fixed thresholds: reproducible and auditable, the only one that does not move when the data does, and the only one that needs someone to have chosen the numbers. `kmeans` clusters both channels at once and names the clusters by where they sit, so it adapts to the well, and it CANNOT abstain because k-means partitions everything. `knn` classifies against a well you have already labelled and abstains into `Rain` when the neighbour vote is weaker than a floor you set, so it is the only one that can decline per droplet. They disagree on the droplets between the populations, and that disagreement is the honest measure of how much an answer rests on the method rather than on the data. Distinct from `gate_droplets`, which asks whether a droplet is EMPTY per channel and ends in a concentration; this asks which of four populations it belongs to. For ONE to FOUR targets multiplexed by amplitude, ddPCRclust names up to sixteen populations from the primary clusters and reports each target's copies per droplet, by any of three first clusterings or their consensus: `density` places the primaries from density gates, `samspectral` from spectral clustering of a faithful sample, `flowpeaks` from the density peaks k-means clusters climb to, and `ensemble` (ddPCRclust's own default) runs all three and keeps the partition that agrees most with the others, with their mean corrected Rand index as the confidence. A plate of exports with ddPCRclust's run template is classified well by well and can be normalised to a constant control.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

ch1_nn.description: grid: Ch1 below this and Ch2 below `ch2_nn` is NN. Only applies when method is grid.

ch1_np.description: grid: Ch1 below this and Ch2 above `ch2_np` is NP. Only applies when method is grid.

ch1_pn.description: grid: Ch1 above this and Ch2 below `ch2_pn` is PN. Only applies when method is grid.

ch1_pp.description: grid: Ch1 above this and Ch2 above `ch2_pp` is PP. Only applies when method is grid.

ch2_nn.description: grid: the Ch2 half of the NN box. Only applies when method is grid.

ch2_np.description: grid: the Ch2 half of the NP box. Only applies when method is grid.

ch2_pn.description: grid: the Ch2 half of the PN box. Only applies when method is grid.

ch2_pp.description: grid: the Ch2 half of the PP box. Only applies when method is grid.

constant_control.description: for a PLATE under the ddPCRclust methods: the marker that should read the same in every well. Every well's copies per droplet are multiplied by the control's highest value on the plate over its own, as `calculateCPDs(constantControl =)` does. Empty: no normalisation. Only applies when method is density or samspectral or flowpeaks or ensemble.

distance_param.description: for `density`: the share of the path between two clusters within which rain goes to the LOWER one; the rest goes to the higher one. Only applies when method is density or samspectral or flowpeaks or ensemble.

droplets.description: the well to classify: two amplitude columns, `Ch1` then `Ch2`, one row per droplet. A header line is optional. This is the whole well, not a summary. For the ddPCRclust methods it may instead be a PLATE: each export as `# <file name>` then its CSV, separated by a line of `---`, the well id read from the file name (`..._B01_Amplitude.csv`).

k.description: for `knn`: how many nearest labelled neighbours vote. Only applies when method is knn.

markers.description: for `density`: the well's four marker slots, comma-separated, as in ddPCRclust's run template. A name is a target the reaction carries; an EMPTY slot is one it does not, so `a,,c,d` is a three-target well whose cluster 2 is missing. The number of names is the number of targets. Only applies when method is density or samspectral or flowpeaks or ensemble.

method.description: which classifier. `grid` needs its eight thresholds to suit your assay; `kmeans` needs nothing and cannot abstain; `knn` needs `training` and is the only one that can leave a droplet unassigned; `density`, `samspectral`, `flowpeaks` and `ensemble` (ddPCRclust) are for one to four targets and name populations by marker number (`1`, `1+2`, ...); `ensemble` runs the other three and is the slowest.

prob.description: for `knn`: the smallest winning share of the vote that counts as a call. Below it the droplet is `Rain`. 0 disables the floor. At k = 5 a bare 3-2 majority is 0.6, so any floor at or below 0.5 accepts every droplet the vote decided at all. Only applies when method is knn.

random_seed.description: for `knn`: ties among equidistant neighbours, and among tied winning classes, are broken from this stream. On a well-separated plate it changes nothing; where droplets sit exactly between populations it does, and a deterministic tie-break would be stable and wrong. Only applies when method is knn.

sam_seed.description: for `samspectral` and `ensemble`: R's `set.seed` before the run. SamSPECTRAL keeps the best of 1000 k-means starts drawn from it, and on a plate one stream runs through the wells in order, as `ddPCRclust()` does. Only applies when method is samspectral or ensemble.

sensitivity.description: for `density`: how finely the initial cluster search resolves density peaks (its step is 0.02 / sensitivity³). Higher divides the data into more clusters, lower merges more. Only applies when method is density or samspectral or flowpeaks or ensemble.

template.description: for a PLATE under the ddPCRclust methods: ddPCRclust's run template (a `>name, channel1=..., channel2=..., description` line, then `Well,Sample type,# of markers,Marker 1..Marker 4`). Each well then takes its own row's markers instead of `markers`. Only applies when method is density or samspectral or flowpeaks or ensemble.

training.description: for `knn` only: an already-labelled well, as `Ch1,Ch2,class` with class one of NN, NP, PN, PP or Rain. Rain IS a class here and not a rejection — a droplet can be assigned to it on the strength of its neighbours, separately from the probability floor below. Only applies when method is knn.

name: classify_droplets

centres.description: for `kmeans`: the final cluster centres with the name geometry gave each one; for `density`: the primary cluster centres, named by marker. Empty for the other methods, which have no centres

classes.description: one label per droplet, in the order given: NN, NP, PN, PP, or Rain where the method abstained

confidence.description: for the ddPCRclust methods: the mean corrected Rand index between the member partitions (1 when one member answered). Low means the three first clusterings disagree about this well

copies_per_droplet.description: for the ddPCRclust methods on one well: each named marker's positive droplets (every population carrying it) and its copies per droplet, -ln(1 - positives / total). Empty for the two-target methods

counts.description: droplets per class, which is what a copy-number read consumes next. Rain is reported separately and is never folded into a population

members.description: for the ddPCRclust methods: each first clustering that ran, with its population counts or the error that left it out of the consensus. `ensemble` is only as good as the members that agreed

method.description: which classifier produced this. A classification without its method is not comparable with another, because the three disagree on the droplets between populations

normalised.description: for a PLATE with `constant_control`: every well's copies per droplet after scaling to the control's highest value on the plate, with each well's factor. Null without a control

params.description: every parameter the run used, defaults included: the thresholds, k and the floor each move the answer

total.description: droplets classified — the denominator the counts sum to

wells.description: for a PLATE: every well's counts, copies per droplet, confidence and members, or the reason no member could partition it. `classes`, `counts` and `total` are empty for a plate
